pictures.title: Webb’s First Deep Field
pictures.about: The galaxy cluster SMACS 0723, 4.6 billion light-years away, in a patch of sky the size of a grain of sand held at arm’s length. The cluster’s mass bends the light of far older galaxies behind it into arcs. Webb’s first full-colour picture, from 12.5 hours of exposure.
pictures.alt: Thousands of galaxies on a black sky, some stretched into thin orange arcs around a cluster of pale galaxies, with a few bright stars showing eight spikes.

pictures.title: The Cosmic Cliffs in Carina
pictures.about: The edge of a young star-forming region, NGC 3324, in the Carina Nebula, about 7,600 light-years away. The light and winds of hot stars above the frame carve the cloud; its tallest peaks are about 7 light-years high. Infrared light shows stars the dust hides in visible light.
pictures.alt: A ragged orange-brown wall of gas and dust like a mountain range, under a deep blue sky full of stars.

pictures.title: The Southern Ring Nebula
pictures.about: NGC 3132, about 2,500 light-years away: shells of gas and dust thrown off by a dying star, here in near-infrared light. Of the two stars at its centre, the fainter made the nebula; Webb’s mid-infrared camera showed it for the first time, wrapped in dust.
pictures.alt: An oval nebula, pale blue within ragged rings of orange, a bright star at its centre, on a black sky.
pictures.credit: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, and the Webb ERO Production Team

pictures.title: Stephan’s Quintet
pictures.about: Five galaxies close together on the sky. Four, about 290 million light-years away, pull at one another, trailing tails of gas and stars and driving a shock wave through the group; the fifth, on the left, is far nearer, at 40 million. A mosaic of more than 150 million pixels.
pictures.alt: Five galaxies, four of them tangled together with red and gold clouds between them, against many faint distant galaxies.

pictures.title: The Pillars of Creation
pictures.about: Columns of cool gas and dust in the Eagle Nebula, 6,500 light-years away, made famous by Hubble in 1995. In near-infrared light the pillars turn half transparent, and the newborn stars at their edges show: the red glow at their tips is from stars still forming.
pictures.alt: Three tall brown and orange columns of dust rising against a blue field crowded with stars.
pictures.credit: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI; J. DePasquale, A. Koekemoer, A. Pagan (STScI)

pictures.title: The heart of the Phantom Galaxy
pictures.about: The spiral galaxy M74, about 32 million light-years away in Pisces, seen face on in mid-infrared light. Filaments of gas and dust wind out along its arms, and its centre, clear of gas, shows the cluster of stars at its core.
pictures.alt: A spiral of fine grey and white filaments winding around a bright blue centre.
pictures.credit: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, J. Lee and the PHANGS-JWST Team. Acknowledgement: J. Schmidt

pictures.title: The Cartwheel Galaxy
pictures.about: A galaxy about 500 million light-years away in Sculptor, with two smaller companions. A smaller galaxy passed through its middle, and two rings spread from the collision like ripples on a pond; the outer ring has been growing for about 440 million years, forming stars as it goes.
pictures.alt: A galaxy like a wheel, a bright hub joined by red spokes to a pink and blue rim, with two small galaxies to its left.

pictures.title: Neptune and its rings
pictures.about: Neptune in near-infrared light, where it is not blue: methane in its air absorbs that light, and only its high clouds of methane ice shine. The clearest view of its rings since Voyager 2 flew past in 1989.
pictures.alt: A pale glowing globe with bright streaks of cloud, circled by thin faint rings and a few small moons.
